To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

soy milk and soy milk supplemented with low dose glyphosate can cause endocrine disruption, and that soy milk with high dose glyphosate can also induce testicular toxicity and decrease in sperm parameters.

the prepubertal exposure of male rats to soy milk supplemented with a low dose (50 mg/kg) of glyphosate leads to decrease in testosterone levels and Sertoli cells number, and increase in the degenerated Sertolil and Leydig cells.
prepubertal subacute exposure to soy milk with or without glyphosate leads to decrease in testosterone levels and to endocrine disruption in male rats.

prepubertal sub chronic exposure to soy milk with glyphosphate (both doses) leads to endocrine disruptor effects, and soy milk without glyphosate also leads to some endocrine disruptor events.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
soy milk supplemented with a glyphosate dose of 100 mg kg ^{−1} during prepuberty period is able to disrupt endocrine function in adult male rats.
soy milk supplemented with low or high doses of glyphosate can cause endocrine disruption, and the effect is more evident in animals receiving soy with high dose of glyphosate.   1
soy milk, when supplemented with glyphosate, leads to endocrine and reproductive disruption in prepubertal male rats, even at doses lower than those found in commercial soy milk.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the consumption of soy milk supplemented with low doses of glyphosate may lead to endocrine disruption and reproductive toxicity.
soy milk consumption in children with lactose intolerance can cause hormonal and testicular alterations.
soy milk, supplemented or not with glyphosphate, is not a suitable substitute for milk during prepubertality.
